chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) — similar to it is like it.
Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
Ibrahim is alleging that the wergild (blood money) of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian is the same. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, he said the truth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for Jews, Christians, and Magians according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (and previously cited by Imam al-Sadiq) confirms the equality of blood money (diyah) among Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians in Islamic jurisprudence, validating Ibrahim's assertion. It highlights the consistency of the Ahl al-Bayt's legal rulings on the status of *Ahl al-Kitab* and *Majusi* within the framework of *diyah*, emphasizing their recognized legal personhood in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan Al Reza<sup>asws</sup> – similat to it’.

Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>,
‘Ibrahim is alleging that the wergild of the Jews, and the Christians, and the Magians, is the same’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, he said the truth’.
